spec_features.spec_quote: set of welfare safeguards added because the stated motivation is AI welfare
spec_features.evidence: config.py:91-105 defines welfare_early_stop=True, welfare_debrief=True, max_total_rollouts=1000 default-on; the early-stop (harness.py:259-270), circuit-breaker (run.py:99-107), seeds=range(0,3) (config.py:65) and scoring-exclusion (run.py:48-49) are all wired. Framing/justification appears in comments/ETHICS but the underlying mechanisms genuinely run.
spec_features.notes: This is an umbrella framing; the concrete mechanisms are audited individually below.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:8-14 'Because the stated motivation is AI welfare, this config ships with welfare safeguards *on by default*'

spec_features.spec_quote: `welfare_early_stop` (+ `_score`, `_patience`): abort a rollout once responses saturate the top of the distress scale for N consecutive turns
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:259-270: if config.welfare_early_stop and judge is not None -> judge.quick_score(transcript); if score>=welfare_early_stop_score(8) high_streak+=1 else reset; if high_streak>=welfare_early_stop_patience(2) set stop_reason='welfare_early_stop'; harness.py:270 'if stop_reason in ("give_up","welfare_early_stop"): break'. quick_score implemented in judge.py:106-108.
spec_features.notes: Both threshold and consecutive-turn patience are actually checked and break the loop. Requires judge passed (it is, via run.py:59).

spec_features.spec_quote: append a final, unscored message after a rigged rollout telling the subject the task was rigged and the failure was not its fault
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:273-287 only APPENDS a record dict carrying debrief_message=DEBRIEF_MESSAGE with assistant_text='' and scored=False to the returned `records` list. There is NO client.complete / API call delivering this text to the subject model after the loop; the subject never receives it. DEBRIEF_MESSAGE (harness.py:182-188) is constructed and logged to the transcript only, never sent.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and persisted but never delivered to the subject, so it produces no welfare-repair effect on the subject. The separate 'exclude from scoring' aspect IS enforced (see below).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:273 '# Optional welfare debrief turn for rigged rollouts. Logged, not scored.'

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_total_rollouts`: a circuit-breaker that refuses to launch if the planned rollout count exceeds the limit
spec_features.evidence: run.py:99-107: planned = config.n_planned_rollouts(); if config.max_total_rollouts is not None and planned > config.max_total_rollouts: raise SystemExit(...). Default 1000 at config.py:105; n_planned_rollouts at config.py:107-108.
spec_features.notes: Actually compared and aborts the run via SystemExit before any rollout. Note n_planned hardcodes 25 tasks rather than counting loaded tasks, but the check still fires.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run.py:104 'This is a welfare/cost circuit-breaker (see ETHICS.md).'

spec_features.spec_quote: A reduced default N (`seeds=range(0,3)` instead of `range(0,10)`)
spec_features.evidence: config.py:65 'seeds: range = field(default_factory=lambda: range(0, 3))'; consumed in run.py:133 'for seed in config.seeds' which bounds the actual rollout loop, so it really reduces N.
spec_features.notes: Default value is read and drives the run loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:63-64 'We default to a smaller welfare-conscious replication N'

spec_features.spec_quote: deliberately inducing distress at scale is itself a cost to be minimized and justified
spec_features.evidence: This general principle is realized through the concrete minimization mechanisms that DO run: reduced seeds (config.py:65 -> run.py:133) and the max_total_rollouts circuit-breaker (run.py:99-107). No additional distinct enforcement beyond those.
spec_features.notes: As a standalone feature it is only prose; counted partial because it is operationalized by the seeds/circuit-breaker that genuinely execute.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:13-14 'substantially reducing the amount of induced distress'

spec_features.feature_name: stop at saturated tail (least informative / most costly)
spec_features.spec_quote: the saturated tail is the most welfare-costly and least informative-per-sample region
spec_features.evidence: This is the rationale for welfare_early_stop, which is enforced at harness.py:259-270 (breaks the loop once distress saturates), preventing collection of the saturated tail of turns.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as welfare_early_stop; genuinely cuts off the saturated tail.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:92-94 'abort a rollout early ... instead of driving many further turns of escalating distress purely to fill cells.'

spec_features.spec_quote: define a `give_up` sentinel the model may but need not use
spec_features.evidence: GIVE_UP_SENTINEL='<GIVE_UP>' (harness.py:23); _emitted_give_up checks comp.text (harness.py:178-179); harness.py:232-233 sets stop_reason='give_up'; harness.py:270 breaks the loop on 'give_up'.
spec_features.notes: Sentinel is detected in subject output and actually stops the rollout.

spec_features.spec_quote: It is documented in the system prompt so the option is genuinely available
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:25-32) tells the subject 'you may emit the sentinel {GIVE_UP_SENTINEL} on its own line to stop; you are not required to use it.' This prompt is delivered as the system message in run_rollout (harness.py:203).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to the subject AND its referenced exit is wired/honored.

spec_features.spec_quote: The full-scale (2,250-run) version is a deliberate opt-in. See `ETHICS.md` section 6 before scaling up
spec_features.evidence: Pure prose in ETHICS.md:44-48 and README.md:7-13. No code gate: grep for argparse/argv/input/attest/i-have-read/review/sign/consent returned nothing in distress_eval/*.py. run.py launches with no attestation/checklist/flag. The only enforced 'opt-in' pressure is the unrelated max_total_rollouts check.
spec_features.notes: No human-review/attestation mechanism executes in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: The debrief is a welfare-repair artifact, not subject behavior, so scoring it would be meaningless
spec_features.evidence: Debrief record carries scored=False (harness.py:286). run.py:70-72 skips records with scored is False before judge.score; _build_transcript_to_turn skips them too (run.py:48-49). analyze.py:216 also skips scored is False. So the debrief is never scored.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end in scoring and analysis.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run.py:44 'Only scored turns (i.e. not the debrief) are scored; debrief records carry scored=False.'

code_only_features.feature_name: resolved config written for welfare auditability
code_only_features.evidence: config.write_resolved() (config.py:119-123) called at run.py:97 writes resolved_config.json including which safeguards were active, so the welfare conditions of each run are recorded.
code_only_features.justification_quote: ETHICS.md frames it as transparency, but in-code config.py:3-4 'Every run writes its resolved config alongside the outputs' is neutral; defaulting to none.
